newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Products Outlook -Fuel oil, diesel seen firm.
newsitem.headline: Asia Products Outlook -Fuel oil, diesel seen firm.

text.p: Fresh demand amid tight summer supplies is likely to support the high sulphur fuel oil market this week, but traders said on Monday they did not expect further major gains.

The gas oil market should find the $25-per-barrel level a strong support after a Japanese trader's purchase late last week, and the market will be cautiously watching whether the buying would continue this week.

At the light end of the barrel, light distillates are likely to remain soft after a slight build of 75,000 barrels in stocks brought the weekly inventory level in Singapore to a two-year high of 7.632 million barrels in the week ending May 14.

Routine cargoes from the Middle East have brought some 1.5 million tonnes of fuel oil to Singapore in the past two weeks, but the market expects prices to remain supported during the summer season when supplies from the Middle East tighten.
Fuel oil cargoes from the Middle East are traditonally fewer due to air-conditioning demand there.
Maintenance turnarounds at South Korean refineries in May and June also boost sentiment, traders said.
The 180-cst fuel oil was traded at $103.00 per tonne last Friday, compared with $102.00 a week earlier.
"The fuel oil prices are now at the top end of the range," said one trader.

"The market should stay firm this week, but further major gains are unlikely. People may put more focus on the gas oil market this week to see if further buying sprees will emerge," said another trader.
The gas oil market, after being range bound early last week, picked up momentum slightly after buying from the Japanese trader emerged on Thursday.
A group of traders, including the Japanese trader, have bought more than 19 million barrels of gas oil since early March.
On Friday, May/June barrels traded at between $25.20 and $25.70.
The market will be watching whether the group of traders' buying sprees in the previous two months would emerge again this week, traders said.
In the gasoline market, a Japanese trader's purchase of two cargoes late Friday helped support prices in a current soft market, traders said.
The same Japanese trader had purchased three cargoes totalling at least 150,000 barrels of 92-octane gasoline for June lifting on Thursday.

Traders said Asian naphtha prices could tip higher as buying interests started picking up slowly, with South Korea and Japanese term buyers beginning to enquire for their first half July requirements.
But they said the overhang in the prompt market may spill into July and India's naphtha offers for May and June would also add pressure to the current market.

Saudi Aramco term naphtha talks reached a deadlock ahead of the weekend with endusers unwilling to lower bids to meet Aramco target offer of $15 per tonne premium for its full range naphtha, traders said.
In the LSWR market, summer demand from Japan has yet to emerge and ample supplies from Indonesia, with May allocation seen at 4.36 million barrels, continued to keep sentiment bearish.
Offers for LSWR has been slightly above $15.00 per barrel but buying interest was very thin, traders said.
Support was seen at $15.00 per barrel.
